gloss: Seir, the hill country of the Horites and later of Esau
note: Filed under the place name’s own consonants. Genesis 14:6 establishes its geographical sense but gives no etymology.
summary: Genesis 14:6 names Seir as the Horites’ hill country. Genesis 36:8 records that Esau settled there, and Deuteronomy 2:12 recalls the Horites as its former inhabitants.

senses.definition: The mountainous territory where the Horites lived and where Esau later settled.

evidence.note: Seir names the hill country in which the attackers struck the Horites.
The verse names the Horites as the former inhabitants of Seir and says that Esau’s descendants displaced them.
